campaign_spec.critical_open_problem: Can large-scale ordering be shown to arise primarily from asymmetric relational dynamics rather than from favorable topology/coherence propagation effects?

hypothesis.statement: Large-scale relational ordering is a causal consequence of the orientation-mediated asymmetric relational compass -(i_a); favorable topology acts only as an amplifier, not a primary driver. In the absence of node asymmetry, even optimal topologies fail to generate persistent ordering fields.

test_design_decoupled_control.description: Systematically isolate asymmetry from topology by testing four configuration quadrants.

quadrants.name: Symmetric / Optimal Topology
quadrants.prediction: Coherence collapse or noise dominance (Critical Falsification).

quadrants.name: Asymmetric / Random Topology
quadrants.prediction: Emergent local ordering despite unfavorable topology (Evidence for hypothesis).

vectors.name: Topology Dominance Test
vectors.attack: Use perfectly ordered lattice with symmetric D(S1|S2)=D(S2|S1).
vectors.failure_condition: System generates persistent large-scale ordering field without asymmetry.
vectors.implication: Topology is a primary driver, falsifying the asymmetry-first hypothesis.

vectors.name: Orientation Reference Scramble
vectors.attack: Maintain asymmetry but continuously randomize -(i_a) orientation references.
vectors.implication: Asymmetry alone is insufficient; orientation mediation is required.

vectors.name: Zero-Residue High-Asymmetry
vectors.attack: Maximum asymmetry but zero residue persistence (R=0).
vectors.failure_condition: Large-scale ordering fields are stable and persistent.
vectors.implication: Asymmetry is necessary but residue is not required for persistence, contradicting the MPF closure model.

success_metrics.correlation_requirement: Asymmetry-to-Ordering correlation > 0.8; Topology-to-Ordering correlation < 0.4 (when asymmetry is fixed).

maximum_supported_claim.statement: Large-scale ordering is causally driven by orientation-mediated asymmetric relational dynamics; favorable topology is a secondary amplifier that cannot sustain ordering in the absence of node asymmetry.
